Well, yeah, I've had times like that before. Like that one a few weeks ago... at first, I felt so fired up, you know? Like I was almost unstoppable. Well, this whole... this whole change, you know? From being so wound up and restless, and then hearing my name called out when no one was there, and then finally just crashing... that whole cycle has been going on for about three weeks now. 

Three weeks... it feels like it's been a lifetime, honestly. I was looking at the calendar in the kitchen the other day to try and figure out exactly when it started. We have one of those big wall calendars with pictures of national parks. This month is Yosemite. I've always wanted to go to Yosemite, or maybe Yellowstone. My uncle went to Yellowstone back in the nineties and brought back all these pictures of Old Faithful. He said it smelled terrible, like rotten eggs, because of the sulfur. He always had a weird sense of smell, though. He claimed he could smell rain coming two days before a storm. I think it was just his bad knee acting up. He broke it playing football in high school and it never healed right. He used to wear this ugly beige knee brace under his slacks, and you could always hear the velcro ripping when he sat down at the Thanksgiving table. We always had Thanksgiving at his house because he had the biggest dining room. His wife made the driest turkey, though. You had to drown it in gravy just to choke it down. I make a much better turkey. I brine mine for 24 hours in apple cider and peppercorns. It keeps it so juicy... but, um... what was the question? Oh, right, how long it lasts. Well, yeah, I did have a few days where I felt totally fired up. Like, almost unstoppable. I was so focused on my craft business and getting the house rules set up perfectly. But then my husband would make some tiny little comment, and I'd just snap at him, like he was trying to hold me back or something. 

My crafts take up a lot of space in the living room right now. I do a lot of resin pouring, making those custom coasters with dried flowers inside. You have to be really careful with the resin, though, because if the room isn't exactly the right temperature, it won't cure properly and it just stays sticky forever. I ruined a whole batch of these beautiful pressed pansies last month because I left the window open. Pansies are my favorite flower. They look like they have little faces on them, you know? My mom used to plant them in these big terra cotta pots on our front porch when I was a kid. But she always bought the cheap potting soil from the hardware store, and it was full of gnats. I hate gnats. They just swarm around your face and you can't ever swat them away. We had a huge problem with them at work last week in the produce section. Some customer left a half-eaten peach on one of the shelves behind the cereal boxes, and it just sat there rotting until someone finally smelled it. It's disgusting what people do in grocery stores. They just leave their trash wherever they want. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, right, being energetic. Yeah, I had a few days where I was just super fired up about my crafts and the house, but I was so irritable with my husband the whole time.

Normal? I don't... I don't even know what normal is supposed to feel like anymore. I guess maybe? Sometimes there's a break, but it's hard to tell because I'm always worried about when the next thing is going to happen.

Are you serious right now? Are you actually doing this on purpose? You just asked me that! We just talked about this! I feel like I'm losing my mind here, or you're playing some kind of sick joke on me. But... fine. Fine. Usual self. I don't know. Like I just said, I don't even know what my usual self is anymore. The rubber balls always smelled so distinct, like hot tires and dirt. \n\nBut um... sorry, I'm doing it again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, crashing. Yeah, I just sit at that oak table and cry. It's just a really heavy, empty feeling.\n\nDoctor: Do you always feel extremely low after one of these energetic periods?\n\nPatient: Are you... are you messing with me? I feel like we're in some kind of time loop here. You just asked me this, didn't you? I swear we just went over this. But... yes. Yes, I do. Like I said, after all that running around and getting so worked up, I just drop into this incredibly heavy, empty feeling. I just sit at my kitchen table and cry over absolutely nothing. I just can't get myself back to normal.\n\nThat table, though... I really need to polish it. The wood is getting so dry. I bought this special beeswax polish from a farmer's market last fall, but I keep forgetting to use it. The farmer's market was great, though. They had these huge Honeycrisp apples. I tried to make an apple pie, but the crust got all soggy on the bottom. Mary, my neighbor, says you have to blind-bake the crust first, but who has time for that? Mary always has time for everything. She's retired and just gardens all day. She has these massive hydrangeas that change color depending on the soil. I think it's the acidity? Or maybe the aluminum in the soil. I don't know, chemistry was never my strong suit. I barely passed it in high school. Mr. Henderson was the teacher, and he always had chalk dust on his pants. \n\nWait, I'm sorry. I'm rambling again. What were we talking about? Oh, the low periods. Yeah, I just sit at that table and cry. It's just awful.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you return to a completely normal mood between these energetic periods?\n\nPatient: Normal? I don't... Like at work, I'm always checking the inventory lists three times because they switched us to this new digital scanner system last month. The old scanners had actual buttons, which I liked better. You could feel the click. These new ones are all touch screens, and if your hands are even a little bit dusty from the cardboard boxes, it doesn't register. That screeching noise they make when you pull the tape... it sounds exactly like a seagull. We went to the beach a lot when I was a kid, down in Florida. The seagulls there would literally swoop down and steal french fries right out of your hand if you weren't paying attention. My sister lost half a hot dog to one once. She screamed so loud. \n\nBut um, normal mood. Yeah, I don't know. I guess maybe there are times I feel okay, but it's just... it's all so blurry.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like you're back to your usual self between these energetic periods?\n\nPatient: Are you serious right now? Are you actually doing this on purpose? You just asked me that! We just talked about this! I feel like I'm losing my mind here, or you're playing some kind of sick joke on me. But... fine. Fine. Usual self. I don't know. Like I just said, I don't even know what my usual self is anymore. Maybe there's a break sometimes, but I'm just constantly on edge waiting for the next drop or the next high.\n\nIt's like waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? My grandmother used to say that all the time. \"Waiting for the other shoe to drop.\" She had this massive collection of shoes, actually. Entire closets full of them. She loved those little kitten heels from the sixties. I tried a pair on once when I was a teenager and immediately twisted my ankle. I had to wear this awful ACE bandage for two weeks right before the spring dance. I ended up wearing these chunky black combat boots with my pastel floral dress. It looked ridiculous, but honestly, it was kind of a look. My friend Sarah did the same thing in solidarity. Sarah was great. We lost touch after she moved to Oregon, though. Oregon seems so rainy. I don't think I could handle all that rain, it would make my knee hurt constantly. \n\nWait, what did you ask me? Right, my usual self. Yeah, I don't know. I don't think I have a usual self anymore. I tried to plant them in a window box, but the pigeons kept eating the seeds before they could sprout. Pigeons are so bold in the city. They just waddle right up to you like they own the place. I saw one the other day eating a whole slice of pizza. Just dragging it across the sidewalk. I sit at the kitchen table and cry over absolutely nothing. You can't even buy that set anymore because they changed the design and the new ones leak everywhere. I had to get it towed to this place on 4th Street, and the mechanic there—I think his name was Sal—he kept telling me the parts were on backorder. Backorder! I was trying to buy my husband's favorite cereal, the one with the little almond clusters, and they didn't have it for a month. He gets so grumpy when he doesn't have his cereal in the morning.
